claims.claim: Kay reports getting caught up in small tinkerings with the text and dropping more italics at the page-proof stage.
claims.source: Guy Gavriel Kay, Under Heaven tour journal, BrightWeavings
claims.quote: I get caught up in small tinkerings with the text, word

claims.claim: Kay says he uses punctuation variably depending on context, speaker and rhythms.
claims.source: Guy Gavriel Kay, Ysabel journal, BrightWeavings
claims.quote: I’ll use punctuation varaibly depending on context, speaker, rhythms.
claims.page: entry on the proofreader over-punctuating speech (the misspelling is the source's)

claims.claim: Kay states that The Last Light of the Sun is punctuated differently from the Sarantine Mosaic.
claims.source: Guy Gavriel Kay, Ysabel journal, BrightWeavings
claims.quote: LAST LIGHT is punctuated differently than the MOSAIC was.
claims.page: entry on the proofreader over-punctuating speech

claims.claim: Kay says he has certain characters speak rapidly under stress.
claims.source: Guy Gavriel Kay, Ysabel journal, BrightWeavings
claims.quote: I have certain characters speaking rapidly at times, under stress
claims.page: entry on the proofreader over-punctuating speech

claims.claim: Kay says italics look louder in galleys than on his screen and he consistently deletes them there.
claims.source: Guy Gavriel Kay, Ysabel journal, BrightWeavings
claims.quote: italics look LOUDER in galleys than they do on my computer
claims.page: entry on deleting italics in the galleys

claims.claim: Kay accepts that a colon better sets off the list that follows in his opening sentence.
claims.source: Guy Gavriel Kay, Ysabel journal, BrightWeavings
claims.quote: a colon better sets off the ‘list’ that follows
claims.page: entry on the copy-editor's query about the Prologue's first sentence

claims.claim: Kay reports deleting the word 'taste' after his copy-editor found the sustained metaphor tangled.
claims.source: Guy Gavriel Kay, Ysabel journal, BrightWeavings
claims.quote: the sentence simply read better after deleting the word ‘taste’

claims.claim: Kay describes copy-editors changing some semi-colons to colons or commas when an author overuses them.
claims.source: Guy Gavriel Kay, Ysabel journal, BrightWeavings
claims.quote: If an author is overusing semi-colons they change some to colons

claims.claim: Kay says Ysabel carries a tag quotation at the end of the book as The Last Light of the Sun did.
claims.source: Guy Gavriel Kay, Ysabel journal, BrightWeavings
claims.quote: it also has a tag quote at the end, as LAST

claims.claim: Wolfe reports Kay's distinction that stories are told but novels are shaped.
claims.quote: Stories, he reminds us, are told, but novels are shaped.

claims.claim: The reviewer notes that Kay's other viewpoints are in third person and so read as immediately distinct from Danio's first-person musings.
claims.quote: these are presented in third person, so they are immediately distinct
claims.page: paragraph beginning 'Danio’s reflections are the major POV'

claims.claim: The reviewer, a self-described completist fan, says Kay's books tend towards a certain sameness.
claims.quote: his books tend towards a certain… sameness

claims.claim: The reviewer lists the recurring archetypes Kay works with as the poet, the warrior, the artist, the lover and the priest.
claims.quote: He works with archetypes — the poet, the warrior, the artist

claims.claim: Fantasy-Faction writes that Kay's writing is lyrical without being flowery.
claims.source: Fantasy-Faction, 'The World of Guy Gavriel Kay', 2011
claims.quote: His writing is lyrical without being flowery.
claims.page: paragraph beginning 'In spite of frequently hitting Canada’s bestseller lists'

claims.claim: Salon Futura describes Written on the Dark as a series of vignettes from Thierry's life rather than a unifying plot.
claims.source: Salon Futura, review of Written on the Dark, April 2025
claims.quote: a series of vignettes – key moments from Thierry’s life that
claims.page: paragraph beginning 'The other thing I should note'
